text:
Ava: Quick heads-up — we need a tight 1-pager for the enterprise launch + the webinar next month. Primary audience: security-minded platform leads. Must cover SLAs, deploy modes (hosted / dedicated / private), and a short benchmark narrative we can use on the webinar slide. Draft by EOD Friday. Any strong opinions on structure or must-have callouts?
Sam: Operator-first structure works well: 1) TL;DR (one-sentence value prop + decision flow), 2) benchmark snapshot (3 scenarios), 3) SLA & security bullets, 4) field play (what to ask in discovery + routing rules), 5) CTAs (PoC request form, architecture checklist). Keep copy tight.
Priya: Agree. For security section pls explicitly call out KMS/HSM integrations, VPC peering options, audit logs retention, and default data-at-rest encryption policy. Also include a one-liner on compliance certifications we support (SOC2 / ISO/PCI note).
Miguel: Sales perspective — add a 3-line ‘Ask’ for field: expected QPS, regulatory constraints, timeline to production. Also a short lead routing rule: if buyer selects "regulated" OR requests private deployment -> route to Enterprise SDR queue, otherwise to Growth. That cut the bounce time.
Jordan: I can mock the 1-pager layout in Figma. Can someone drop the exact benchmark numbers we want to show (p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens) or should I use placeholders? Fig link: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/redwood-enterprise-1pager
Sam: Benchmark narrative suggestion (to be converted to a 2-row visual):
- Scenario A (low-latency chat): 8k context, p50 gen latency 150ms, p95 280ms, cost delta vs baseline model: -30% with RT-quantization.
- Scenario B (high-throughput embeddings): 5M requests/day, batched throughput 120k embeddings/min, unit cost $0.0007/embed, cache hit reduces marginal cost by 45%.
- Scenario C (bursty document processing): sustained burst to 200 concurrent streams, fallback to dedicated pool keeps 99.9% success with <1% degraded responses.
Use these as illustrative numbers and mark as "based on internal workload simulations".
Priya: Add a short note on graceful degradation: describe automatic routing to fallback model variant + region failover + notification to ops. That's a big buyer concern.
Miguel: For webinar CTA: prefer a short form with 4 fields only: company, role, use-case (dropdown: chat/embed/batch), urgency (ASAP/1-3 months/6+ months). If "regulatory" selected -> trigger Enterprise SDR and include a checkbox for wanting an architecture review.
Ava: Good. For the one-pager copy, keep it single-column printable. Jordan — include an expandable section for the benchmark graph and a small decision flow diagram for deploy mode selection.
Ava: Quick routing snippet for the ops/playbook section (small pseudo-yaml for field):
```
route_rules:
  - when: "lead.use_case == 'regulated' or lead.deployment == 'private'"
    action: "route_to: enterprise-sdr"
  - when: "lead.use_case == 'pilot' and lead.qps > 1000"
    action: "route_to: solutions-engineering"
  - default: "route_to: growth-sdr"
```
Sam: Love the yaml snippet. We'll also include an in-email quicklink for Sales: `redwood.com/enterprise/one-pager-download?utm=webinar`
Jordan: I'll drop a first Figma draft by Thursday AM. Want to keep the color palette muted and enterprise-first — greens removed, use slate + accent orange for CTAs.
Priya: I'll write the security bullets and the compliance blurb. Miguel — can you mock one example of a routed lead (just a sample form filled) so we can test webhook routing during the webinar?
Miguel: Yep, I'll create 2 samples (regulated+private and quick pilot) and send to the webhook test channel by Thursday.
Ava: Great — owners and deadlines: Jordan (design draft) Thurs AM, Priya (security copy + compliance line) Thurs EOD, Sam (benchmark & slide snippet) Thurs EOD, Miguel (sample leads + routing test) Thurs EOD. I'll assemble the one-pager and publish a final Google Drive PDF by Friday EOD.
Sam: One more small ask — include a one-line ‘what success looks like’ for customers: "<30ms p50 improvement on chat or 40% cost reduction on embedding-heavy workloads" — pick whichever we can truthfully claim.
Ava: Noted — we'll pick the least risky claim. Thanks team :thumbsup: We'll sync again Friday 10am if needed.
